title: Pivot Quarterly Sales into Columns Using CASE
description:
Transform row-level quarterly sales data into a wide format with one column per quarter using conditional aggregation (CASE + GROUP BY).

**Table: sales** — `region`, `quarter`, `amount`

Output columns: `region`, `q1`, `q2`, `q3`, `q4`. Order by `region`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, quarter VARCHAR, amount INT); INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('North','Q1',15000),('North','Q2',18000),('North','Q3',22000),('North','Q4',20000),('South','Q1',12000),('South','Q2',14000),('South','Q3',16000),('South','Q4',19000),('East','Q1',9000),('East','Q2',11000),('East','Q3',13000),('East','Q4',10000);
solution_sql: SELECT region, SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q1' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q1, SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q2' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q2, SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q3' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q3, SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q4' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q4 FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY region

test_cases.description: 12 input rows (3 regions × 4 quarters) collapsed into 3 pivot rows, one per region

hints: Use SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q1' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) to filter each quarter into its own column.
GROUP BY region collapses the 4 quarter rows per region into a single wide row.
explanation: This is the standard SQL PIVOT pattern: for each target column, use a conditional CASE WHEN inside an aggregate function. GROUP BY region turns 4 rows per region into 1. North: q1=15000, q2=18000, q3=22000, q4=20000. South: 12000,14000,16000,19000. East: 9000,11000,13000,10000. No native PIVOT syntax needed.
